name: champion’s portion

attributes.attribute: best share of the meat at the feast

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The champion's portion is a theme in Irish myth. At a feast the foremost warrior received the curad-mir, the choicest share of the meat, often read as the thigh. When two or more warriors claimed the prize, a fight began at once, sometimes to the death. The practice appears in records as old as the first century BCE. Briccriu spoke sharply, and he used this habit to set several champions against each other.

okr.objective: The champion's portion is the prize given to the strongest warrior at a feast.
key_results: The foremost warrior received the curad-mir at the meal.
Two or more warriors who claimed it started to fight.
The custom is recorded from the first century BCE.
Briccriu used the prize to rouse rivalry among champions.
